correctness.rationale: Reconstructed source AWVC strict coalition inequality and finite normalized candidate measure; for each fixed disapprover coalition, the unanimously superior set changes by exactly t*chi, while m changes by t and support stays s. Algebra yields the exact affine nonblocking formula. Since s>n/2>=|S|, all chi=0 constraints have positive slopes and chi=1 have negative slopes. Intersection yields exact integer interval with correct closed endpoints. The five-voter family has precisely three nonempty disapprover coalitions and calculations t<=3h-2, t>=1, t>=7-3h, so t in [1,3h-2]. No circular lemma. Actual check.py independently checked 25,270 finite cases but universal proof is analytical. Boundaries h=2,t=0,1,4,5 and empty/fully-approved cases are handled.

originality.rationale: The identified 2026 defining paper gives the approval-weighted veto block formula, majority threshold, and monotonicity for voter entry, without repeated-alternative-cloning response laws. An older precursor establishes only a qualitative independence-of-clones failure for the ordinary proportional veto core; that phenomenon is fully credited. The claimed theorem is the exact integer clone-count interval for an unchanged majority-supported target under the distinct approval-weighted denominator, and the five-voter construction realizing an arbitrary-length finite acceptance window. Direct and alias-oriented published-literature and mathematical-result searches revealed no equivalent or logically stronger coverage. residual_risks: A more general candidate-insertion theorem in unindexed game-theoretic literature might imply this specific formula.

value.rationale: Clone sensitivity is a central structural robustness question in single-winner social choice and proposal eligibility screening, and already motivates independence-of-clones axioms. The theorem gives a complete quantitative response of a majority-supported target to arbitrary candidate replication; the concrete five-voter exact window is an unbounded form of consent reversal under unchanged voters, preferences over original proposals, approval of the target, and clone origin. These parameter-free political/institutional distinctions are more informative than a one-off toy clone counterexample. Existing qualitative ordinal proportional-veto non-independence is fully acknowledged and does not supply this exact AWVC theorem.
